enqueue_fse_css echoes $style directly without esc_html() or wp_kses_post(), and $css is generated by cycle_through_blocks() without any sanitization, creating an XSS vector through block attribute injection. Additionally, $templates_part->content from get_block_templates() is concatenated into $content without sanitization before being parsed and processed.

WPCS Compliance: severity high (4/10) — Issue: echo $style is explicitly suppressed with phpcs:ignore WordPress.Security.EscapeOutput.OutputNotEscaped, acknowledging the escape violation; the suppression comment does not fix the underlying XSS risk from unsanitized block content.. Fix: Replace echo $style with echo wp_kses_post( $style ) or apply wp_kses_post() to $css before building $style, and sanitize $templates_part->content with wp_kses_post() before concatenating.

SQL Safety: severity low (8/10) — Issue: No SQL queries are executed in enqueue_fse_css; get_block_templates() uses the WP Template API internally.. Fix: No SQL remediation needed.

Security: severity critical (2/10) — Issue: $css is generated by cycle_through_blocks() processing $content, which includes raw $templates_part->content from get_block_templates() without sanitization; a malicious template part could inject arbitrary HTML/JS via block attributes, which cycle_through_blocks() may pass through to the final $css output without escaping.. Fix: Sanitize $templates_part->content with wp_kses_post() before appending to $content, and apply wp_kses_post() to the final $style before echoing.

Performance: severity medium (6/10) — Issue: In the else branch (classic themes), get_block_templates( array(), 'wp_template_part' ) retrieves ALL template parts in the site with no limit, then iterates all of their contents;
